title: Sam's Tower Falls Down
synopsis: A fallen block tower disappoints Sam; after a break and help with one step, he builds a different little house.

related_resources.reason: Caregiver strategies for frustration; not evidence that grit or solitary persistence always works.
Age-adapted play, flexible plans and scaffolding; does not empirically evaluate these particular story manuscripts.
Examples of adult-supported observation and experimentation; not proof that one narrative changes reasoning skills.

rationale_citations.story_anchor: For a while, he didn't want to build anything.
rationale_citations.editorial_rationale: Feeling upset and taking a break are valid responses to difficulty.
rationale_citations.evidence_scope: Caregiver advice to acknowledge frustration and allow breaks, not a clinical intervention.

rationale_citations.story_anchor: Perhaps, Sam thought, it needed a house.
rationale_citations.editorial_rationale: A new goal can be preferable to repeating a failed one indefinitely.
rationale_citations.evidence_scope: Guidance discusses flexible plans in play; narrative solution is invented.

rationale_citations.story_anchor: Sam asked his grown-up to hold one block steady while he tried again.
rationale_citations.editorial_rationale: An adult can help with part of the task while the child remains involved.
rationale_citations.evidence_scope: Neither source requires children to complete tasks without adult help.

source_note: The manuscript is original fictional narrative. Citations apply only to stated parent-facing developmental rationales; they do not source plots or establish an effect from listening to this story.
